attacks.claim: The day card background is hardcoded to white while text uses the dark-mode variable. In dark mode, near-white text (#f2f2f7) sits on a white card, roughly 1.1:1 contrast, so planner content is effectively unreadable for the ~30% of users on dark mode.
attacks.evidence: .day-card { background: #ffffff; color: var(--text); ... } alongside @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root { --text: #f2f2f7; ... } }

attacks.claim: Muted meta text fails WCAG contrast in dark mode because it is placed on the hardcoded white card. #a1a1a6 on #ffffff is about 2.5:1, below the 4.5:1 minimum for body text.
attacks.evidence: .tile .meta { color: var(--muted); } with .day-card { background: #ffffff; }

attacks.claim: QA covers only light mode (Chrome 1440px light, Safari iPhone 14 light). Dark mode, 360px and Android widths, and touch drag are untested, despite the brief stating 68% mobile traffic, 360-414px viewports, and ~30% dark-mode users.
attacks.evidence: Visual QA vs Figma: Chrome 1440px (light), Safari iPhone 14 (light) — pass, pixel diffs < 1%.

attacks.claim: The fixed mobile action bar (72px) overlaps page content. .planner has only 16px bottom padding and Sunday is its last child, so the bottom of the week, including Sunday's recipes, can sit behind the bar on mobile.
attacks.evidence: .action-bar { position: fixed; ... height: 72px; ... } and .planner { ... padding: 16px; ... } with "Sunday is the last child of .planner"

attacks.claim: Adding a recipe's ingredients to the shopping list, the most frequent planner action at 9.4 times per week and 64% on mobile, goes from one tap to a six-step flow. The planner's per-tile "+ List" button is removed, and the bulk action only adds the whole week.
attacks.evidence: The old tile-level "+ List" button is removed to declutter tiles. To add a recipe to the shopping list: tap the tile → recipe page → "Ingredients" tab → choose servings in the servings sheet → "Add to list" → toast with "Undo".

attacks.claim: The redesign optimizes the stated goal (decluttering tiles) at the cost of the top-used workflow. The artifact provides no evidence that the decluttering problem is one users have, and the shopping-list regression is the most likely outcome.
attacks.evidence: Most frequent planner action: adding a planned recipe's ingredients to the shopping list (avg 9.4 times/week per weekly-active user).

attacks.claim: The release goes to 100% of web users at once with no staged ramp or canary, even though the dark-mode and layout defects affect a large share of traffic. The flag rollback is a whole-page switch, and no error or readiness thresholds are defined for rollback.
attacks.evidence: Ship to 100% Tue 10:00 PT behind `planner_v7`

attacks.claim: Watch metrics have no thresholds, alert conditions, or owners, so a regression in shopping-list additions or bounce rate has no defined trigger for flipping the flag off.
attacks.evidence: Watch: planner page JS errors, shopping-list additions/WAU, planner bounce rate.

attacks.claim: A new "Share plan" action is introduced with no specification of what is shared, who can view it, whether links are public or expiring, or whether user consent is needed. Meal plans can expose personal routines.
attacks.evidence: New sticky bottom bar on mobile with "Generate shopping list" (adds all planned recipes for the week) and "Share plan".

attacks.claim: The claim that the old planner works with "same API, no data migration" after the flag flips is asserted, not demonstrated. No rollback test is reported.
attacks.evidence: old planner remains available by flipping the flag off (same API, no data migration)

attacks.claim: "Generate shopping list" adds all planned recipes for the week, but the artifact does not say how it handles recipes already added individually, so duplicate ingredients or double-counted quantities are possible.
attacks.evidence: "Generate shopping list" (adds all planned recipes for the week)

attacks.claim: The bulk action writes ingredients for up to 21 recipes in one action with no described batching, rate limit, or partial-failure handling, so it may be slow or fail partway through.
attacks.evidence: Each day is a `.day-card` with up to 3 recipe tiles (breakfast/lunch/dinner).

attacks.claim: Drag-and-drop is the primary move mechanism and is pointer-based in the markup. Touch drag on mobile is not in the QA scope, and the toast with "Undo" has no described live-region announcement for screen-reader users.
attacks.evidence: Drag a recipe tile between days to move it. ... Drag-and-drop between days ... VoiceOver: pass.

attacks.claim: The "Lighthouse mobile" score does not state the device profile or whether it was run in dark mode, so the 91 performance and 100 accessibility scores cannot be checked against the dark-mode contrast failures.
attacks.evidence: Lighthouse mobile: performance 91, accessibility 100, CLS 0.01.

attacks.claim: `.day-card` hardcodes a white background while text switches to near-white `--text` (#f2f2f7) under `prefers-color-scheme: dark`. For the roughly 30% of users on dark mode, day-card text and headings render almost invisible on white, and the muted meta text is also low-contrast.
attacks.evidence: `.day-card { background: #ffffff; color: var(--text); ... }` vs `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root { --text: #f2f2f7; ... } }`

attacks.claim: QA covers only light mode (Chrome 1440px and iPhone 14 light). Nothing shows dark mode, the 360-414px range where 68% of sessions occur, or non-iPhone Android devices, so the 'pass' claims do not support shipping to 100% of users.
attacks.evidence: "Chrome 1440px (light), Safari iPhone 14 (light) — pass, pixel diffs < 1%."

attacks.claim: Adding a recipe to the shopping list, the most frequent planner action at 9.4 times per week and 64% on mobile, goes from one tap to a five-step flow. The change removes the tile-level '+ List' button with no replacement shortcut on the planner.
attacks.evidence: "The old tile-level "+ List" button is removed to declutter tiles." / "tap the tile → recipe page → "Ingredients" tab → choose servings in the servings sheet → "Add to list" → toast with "Undo""

attacks.claim: The redesign optimizes for decluttering at the cost of the most-used action, which the brief's own data identifies. The proposal does not show that users asked for less clutter or that the removal improves the planner's core task.
attacks.evidence: "Most frequent planner action: adding a planned recipe's ingredients to the shopping list (avg 9.4 times/week per weekly-active user)."

attacks.claim: On mobile the action bar is `position: fixed` at 72px high, but `.planner` has no bottom padding or spacer. The last day (Sunday) and its tiles can sit under the bar and be unreachable or obscured.
attacks.evidence: "position: fixed; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; height: 72px;" with ".planner { ... padding: 16px; ... }" and "Sunday is the last child of .planner"

attacks.claim: 'Generate shopping list' adds all planned recipes for the week in one action, with no stated dedupe against items already on the list, no confirmation, and no undo. Repeated taps or a re-run could duplicate ingredients, and the single-add undo does not cover the bulk action.
attacks.evidence: ""Generate shopping list" (adds all planned recipes for the week)"; undo is only specified for "Add to list" → toast with "Undo"

attacks.claim: Several 'Swap' buttons repeat the same label with no recipe name, so screen-reader users hearing the list cannot tell which recipe each one affects. Tap targets for `.btn-ghost` and `.btn-icon` have no minimum size, unlike the 48px primary button.
attacks.evidence: "<button class="btn-ghost">Swap</button>" and "<button class="btn-icon" aria-label="More options for Sheet-pan gnocchi">⋯</button>" with no min-height

attacks.claim: The rollout goes straight to 100% of web users with no staged canary, and the watch list has no alert thresholds or owner for the named metrics, so a regression in JS errors or shopping-list adds may go unnoticed for a long time.
attacks.evidence: "Ship to 100% Tue 10:00 PT behind `planner_v7`" and "Watch: planner page JS errors, shopping-list additions/WAU, planner bounce rate."

attacks.claim: 'Share plan' is listed with no specification of what it exposes, whether links are unguessable or expiring, or whether the shared plan reveals personal meal data.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: the sharing mechanism, link scope, and expiry for "Share plan"

attacks.claim: `.day-card` hardcodes `background: #ffffff` while text uses `var(--text)`, which switches to light (#f2f2f7) under `prefers-color-scheme: dark`. In dark mode, headings and tile titles render near-white on white cards, and `--muted` meta text (#a1a1a6) is also low contrast. About 30% of users run dark mode, so this hits them at 100% rollout.
attacks.evidence: `.day-card { background: #ffffff; color: var(--text); ... }` alongside `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root { --text: #f2f2f7; ... --surface: #1c1c1e; --page: #000000; } }`

attacks.claim: The mobile action bar is `position: fixed` at 72px height, but `.planner` has no bottom padding to clear it. The last day (Sunday) and its tiles can be hidden behind the bar when scrolled to the end.
attacks.evidence: `.action-bar { position: fixed; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; height: 72px; ... }` and `.planner { ... padding: 16px; ... }`; "Sunday is the last child of .planner"

attacks.claim: The most frequent planner action (about 9.4 shopping-list additions per user per week) goes from one tap to a multi-step flow. The per-tile "+ List" button is removed, and the only bulk alternative adds the whole week at once, so there is no per-recipe quick add.
attacks.evidence: "The old tile-level \"+ List\" button is removed to declutter tiles." and "tap the tile → recipe page → \"Ingredients\" tab → choose servings in the servings sheet → \"Add to list\" → toast with \"Undo\"." versus "Most frequent planner action: adding a planned recipe's ingredients to the shopping list (avg 9.4 times/week...)"

attacks.claim: QA covers only light mode (Chrome 1440px light, Safari iPhone 14 light) and Lighthouse. No dark-mode visual or contrast check is reported, even though the stylesheet changes colors under dark mode and the brief says 30% of users use it. The claim of visual parity is not supported for the dark-mode path.
attacks.evidence: "Visual QA vs Figma: Chrome 1440px (light), Safari iPhone 14 (light) — pass, pixel diffs < 1%."

attacks.claim: The rollout goes to 100% of web users in one step, with no staged cohort. The watch list has no thresholds or alert definitions, and it does not include dark-mode or layout regressions, so a bad release would be detected late.
attacks.evidence: "Ship to 100% Tue 10:00 PT behind `planner_v7`" and "Watch: planner page JS errors, shopping-list additions/WAU, planner bounce rate."

attacks.claim: "Generate shopping list" adds all planned recipes for the week, but the artifact does not say whether repeated taps or re-adding already-listed ingredients are deduplicated or idempotent. This could double-count quantities.
attacks.evidence: "\"Generate shopping list\" (adds all planned recipes for the week)"; no dedupe or idempotency behavior specified

attacks.claim: "Share plan" is a new public-facing action in the sticky bar, but the artifact does not specify what it exposes, whether links are unguessable or revocable, or whether the shared plan includes personal data. This is a possible exposure path with no spec or QA coverage.
attacks.evidence: "New sticky bottom bar on mobile with \"Generate shopping list\" ... and \"Share plan\"."; ABSENT: sharing scope, link visibility, revocation, QA of share flow
